subject: Cluster readiness: rack NIC bonding, tape-archive flow, and nodeclass reclamation

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Cluster readiness: rack NIC bonding, tape-archive flow, and nodeclass reclamation

Hi Liam / Helios team,

Thanks for the intake call earlier — following up with a short checklist and a few clarifying questions so we can finalize the on‑prem provisioning playbook for your primary site (RACK‑7). Please see attached site-inventory-template.csv and a high‑level provisioning-outline.pdf.

Key items we need your input on before the sprint kickoff:
- NIC bonding: do you prefer active‑backup or LACP across the two top‑of‑rack switches? Any vendor constraints (Brocade/Cumulus/etc.) we should flag?
- Tape‑archive flow: you mentioned a cold archive on tape for weekly snapshots. Who owns the retrieval workflow (Helios ops vs. third‑party vendor) and what retention window (weeks/months) do you target?
- Nodeclass reclamation: we need your policy for reclaiming CPU‑heavy vs. storage‑heavy nodeclasses (e.g., preempt window, grace period for eviction).
- Storage backend: will NVMe-backed local SSD be primary for caching, with a separate blockstore for long‑term dataset mounts? Any encryption KMS in scope?

Initial assumptions from our side:
- Three control-plane nodes (HA), mixed nodeclasses for gpu/cpu, default CNI with BGP peering to your core.
- Default StorageClass: fast-ephemeral (LocalNVMe), blockstore-standard (iSCSI/Ceph RBD) for persistent model datasets.
- Egress: NAT gateway in the DMZ with strict egress ACLs; we will propose static routes for model pulling from our artifact registry.

Could you confirm the NIC bonding preference and tape retrieval owner by EOD Friday? If helpful, we can schedule a short 30m technical check on Friday morning.

Thanks,
Olga
--

Subject: Re: Cluster readiness: rack NIC bonding, tape-archive flow, and nodeclass reclamation

Hi Olga — great to hear from you. Quick answers below, and we can lock any remaining details on a call.

- NIC bonding: we run Cumulus on the ToR switches and prefer LACP (802.3ad) for aggregated throughput.
- Tape archive: Helios ops will own retrievals. Retention for the weekly model snapshots: 26 weeks (6 months). Retrieval SLA: 24–48 hours for tape recall.
- Nodeclass reclamation: default reclaim window 72 hours after a failed job; for GPU nodeclasses we require 7‑day hold for ephemeral checkpoints unless explicitly cleared.
- Storage backend: local NVMe for hot cache, long‑term mounts on our Ceph RBD cluster; KMS is HashiCorp Vault (separate self‑managed instance).

We're available for a 30m technical sync Friday 10:00–10:30 PT. I can loop in our network engineer if needed.

Regards,
Liam
Liam Carter
Platform Ops Lead, Helios BioResearch
liam.carter@heliosbio.com

Subject: Re: Cluster readiness: rack NIC bonding, tape-archive flow, and nodeclass reclamation

Thanks Liam — LACP makes sense with Cumulus. A couple of technical proposals from my side before the Friday sync:

1) Nodeclass layout (proposal attached: nodeclass-proposal.yaml)
   - control-plane: 3 x m6a.large (dual 10G uplinks, 64GB RAM)
   - cpu-worker: 6 x c5a.4xlarge (48GB, 8 cores) for model preprocess jobs
   - gpu-worker: 4 x p4d-like (for offline fine-tuning) with 2 x 100Gb NICs set LACP
   - storage-nodes: 3 x i3en-style for local NVMe + 8TB HDD for local backups

2) Networking and BGP
   - We'll establish BGP peering between customer leaf and our edge router for model artifact pulls. We'll avoid default route advertisement; only /32s for control-plane and a specific prefix for artifact pull IPs.
   - Egress ACLs: allow outbound to redwood-artifact-registry.redwood.internal:443 and to Vault for KMS operations.

3) Tape archive integration
   - We'll add a weekly job to snapshot model-storage namespace and push to an S3-compatible tape gateway at Helios. Redwood will log every outgoing snapshot (hash + timestamp) to the audit log and retain the local manifest for 6 months.

4) Reclamation automation
   - Proposal: use a reconciliation job that marks GPU node PVCs with annotation redwood/reclaim-hold=true for 7 days; after that TTL controller deletes ephemeral volumes. We'll surface an approval webhook for manual hold extension.

Open questions for the call:
- Who is the network engineer we should expect on Friday so we can do a short BGP handshake?
- Are there any cross‑tenant constraints in your Ceph cluster we should be aware of for volume provisioning?

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
